359610.title: Linear dependence conjecture for Norton algebra vectors
359610.statement: Let $\Gamma=(X,\mathcal R)$ be a distance-regular graph that is $Q$-polynomial with respect to a primitive idempotent $E$. For distinct vertices $x,y\in X$, let $C(x,y)$ and $B(x,y)$ be the vectors appearing in the expression for the Norton algebra product $E\hat{x}\star E\hat{y}$, together with $E\hat{x}+E\hat{y}$. Assume that $\Gamma$ satisfies Assumptions and. **The Norton algebra linear-dependence conjecture.** The vectors $C(x,y)$, $B(x,y)$, and $E\hat{x}+E\hat{y}$ are linearly dependent. The conjecture concerns the structure of the Norton algebra associated with a $Q$-polynomial distance-regular graph; its status is not determined by the supplied text.
359610.source_name: Kazumasa Nomura and Paul Terwilliger, “Spin models and distance-regular graphs of q-Racah type”, arXiv:2308.11061 (2023).
359610.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.11061

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

359659.title: The irreducible-snark defect-3 conjecture
359659.statement:
Let $G$ be an **irreducible snark**, meaning a snark for which deleting any pair of distinct vertices produces a $3$-edge-colourable graph, and let defect denote colouring defect. **Irreducible-snark defect-3 conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{defect}(G)=3.
$$

Irreducible snarks form a subfamily of critical snarks, so this is presented as a weaker consequence of the critical-snark conjectures. Its general status is open.
359659.source_name: Ján Karabáš, Edita Máčajová, Roman Nedela and Martin Škoviera, “Cubic graphs with colouring defect 3”, arXiv:2308.13639 (2023).
359659.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.13639

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2023). “Jaeger conjectured that there exist no (nontrivial) snarks of girth greater than 6, which was later disproved by Kochol in .”

359735.title: Subquotient conjecture for quantum groups under edge contractions
359735.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a graph, let $e$ be an edge of $\Gamma$, and let $\Gamma/e$ denote the graph obtained by contracting $e$. Write $\mathbf U_{\Gamma/e}$ and $\mathbf U_{\Gamma}$ for the associated quantum groups, and let the edge contraction induce the explicit embedding

$$
\mathbf U_{\Gamma/e}\hookrightarrow \mathbf U_{\Gamma}.
$$

**Subquotient conjecture.** The explicit embedding for quantum groups in Theorem~ is a section of a subquotient.
This conjecture is motivated by the corresponding result for Hall algebras and their positive and negative halves; the precise subquotient structure for the full quantum groups is proposed but not established in the supplied text.
359735.source_name: Yiqiang Li, “Quantum groups and edge contractions”, arXiv:2308.16306 (2023).
359735.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.16306

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

359746.title: Jordán and Garamvölgyi's separator conjecture for globally linked pairs
359746.statement: Let $G=G_1\cup G_2$, where $|V(G_1)\cap V(G_2)|\leq d+1$, and let $u,v\in V(G_1)\cap V(G_2)$. A pair is **$\mathcal{R}_d$-linked** when it is contained in an $\mathcal{R}_d$-circuit. **Jordán and Garamvölgyi's separator conjecture.** If $\{u,v\}$ is $\mathcal{R}_d$-linked in both $G_1$ and $G_2$, then $\{u,v\}$ is globally linked in $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The conjecture concerns how global linkage behaves under unions with small separators and remains unresolved in the source.
359746.source_name: Dániel Garamvölgyi, “Stress-linked pairs of vertices and the generic stress matroid”, arXiv:2308.16851 (2025).
359746.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.16851

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2023). “While in Jordán and the author proved the upper bound on the number of edges, the other conjecture remains open.”

359752.title: The area conjecture for grid polygons with holes
359752.statement:
Let $P$ be a grid polygon with holes. Let $\operatorname{cyc}(P)$ denote the number of cycles in its billiards permutation, let $\operatorname{area}(P)$ denote its area, and let $\operatorname{holes}(P)$ denote the number of holes. **The area conjecture for grid polygons with holes.**

$$
\operatorname{cyc}(P) \leq \frac{1}{6}\operatorname{area}(P)+\operatorname{holes}(P)+1.
$$

This is proposed as an area analogue for polygons with holes, complementing the perimeter conjecture after the corresponding hole-free area bound was noted to fail for polygons with holes. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
359752.source_name: Honglin Zhu, “The maximum number of cycles in a triangular-grid billiards system with a given perimeter”, arXiv:2309.00100 (2024).
359752.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00100

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

359985.title: Nonadjacency conjecture for degree-5 vertices in edge-to-edge plane graphs
359985.statement:
Let $EP$ be an edge-to-edge plane graph. A pair of vertices of degree $5$ is called **adjacent** when the two vertices are joined by an edge.

**Nonadjacency conjecture.** Are there any two degree-$5$ vertices adjacent in $EP$? No way! Equivalently, no two degree-$5$ vertices in $EP$ are adjacent.

This conjecture is presented as covering the previous results in the paper, but the authors state that an attempted proof contained a bug and that the claim remains unresolved.
359985.source_name: Shu-Chung Liu, “A renewal approach to prove the Four Color Theorem unplugged, Part III: Diamond routes, canal lines and Σ-adjustments”, arXiv:2309.09998 (2023).
359985.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.09998

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

359992.title: The extension conjecture for non-toric staged tree models
359992.statement: Let $\mathcal T$ be a staged tree with non-toric $V(\ker \varphi_{\mathcal T})$ that uses color set $S$. Let $\mathcal T'$ be a staged tree such that its restriction to color set $S$ gives $\mathcal T$. **Extension conjecture.** Then $\ker \varphi_{\mathcal T'}$ is not toric under any linear change of variables. This conjecture proposes that non-toric structure persists when a staged tree is extended while retaining the original color set. The paper gives no proof or resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
359992.source_name: Aida Maraj and Arpan Pal, “Symmetry Lie Algebras of Varieties with Applications to Algebraic Statistics”, arXiv:2309.10741 (2025).
359992.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.10741

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

360038.title: Density-Ramanujan conjecture for congruence complexes
360038.statement: Let $G$ be a definite Gross inner form and let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a finite place. Let $\{X_{\mathfrak{p}}(q)\}$ denote its family of congruence complexes. **Density-Ramanujan conjecture.** For any definite Gross inner form $G$ and any finite place $\mathfrak{p}$, the family $\{X_{\mathfrak{p}}(q)\}$ forms a family of density-Ramanujan complexes. The source states this as a conjecture about congruence complexes; no resolution is given.
360038.source_name: Shai Evra, Mathilde Gerbelli-Gauthier and Henrik P. A. Gustafsson, “The Cohomological Sarnak-Xue Density Hypothesis for SO_5”, arXiv:2309.12413 (2025).
360038.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.12413

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

360047.title: Dependence of forward Zeckendorf game strategies on reverse game winners
360047.statement: Let the forward and reverse Zeckendorf games be played from corresponding starting positions, with each game having a winning player under optimal play. **Forward–reverse Zeckendorf conjecture.** The winning strategy for the forward Zeckendorf games is dependent upon who wins the reverse Zeckendorf game. This conjecture proposes a relationship between the winning structures of the forward and reversed games; the source does not provide a resolution.
360047.source_name: Zoë X. Batterman, Aditya Jambhale, Steven J. Miller, Akash L. Narayanan, Kishan Sharma, Andrew K. Yang and Chris Yao, “The Reversed Zeckendorf Game”, arXiv:2309.12748 (2023).
360047.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.12748

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

360136.title: The virtual mapping-torus conjecture for negative immersions
360136.statement: A compact $2$-complex $X$ has **negative immersions** when it satisfies the negative-immersion property defined in the source. An **immersion** is a map $\psi:H\rightarrow F$ between graphs, and its **finite directed height** is the finiteness condition on directed intersections associated with the immersion. **The virtual mapping-torus conjecture for negative immersions.** If $X$ is a compact $2$-complex with negative immersions, then $\pi_1X$ has a finite index subgroup isomorphic to the fundamental group of a mapping torus of an immersion $\psi:H\rightarrow F$ of finite directed height. This conjecture proposes that negative immersions force a virtual mapping-torus structure; the source gives no resolution.
360136.source_name: Brahim Abdenbi and Daniel T. Wise, “Negative Immersions and Finite Height Mappings”, arXiv:2309.15961 (2023).
360136.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15961

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

360150.title: Equivalence of componentwise linearity, linear quotients, and vertex splittability for weighted oriented graph edge ideals
360150.statement: Let $D$ be a weighted oriented graph, and let $I(D)$ denote its edge ideal. The properties in question are componentwise linearity of $I(D)$, having linear quotient property, and being a vertex splittable ideal. **Equivalence conjecture.** The following are equivalent: $I(D)$ is componentwise linear; $I(D)$ has linear quotient property; and $I(D)$ is a vertex splittable ideal. The conjecture proposes that these three properties, already known to coincide for several large classes of weighted oriented graphs, are equivalent for the edge ideals of every weighted oriented graph.
360150.source_name: Manohar Kumar, Ramakrishna Nanduri and Kamalesh Saha, “Componentwise linearity of edge ideals of weighted oriented graphs”, arXiv:2309.16810 (2023).
360150.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16810

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

360160.title: Brändén and Huh's matroid characterization by homogeneous $\frac{8}{7}$-Rayleigh polynomials
360160.statement:
Let $J$ be a non-empty subset of $\{0,1\}^{n}$, and let $f_J$ denote its generating function. A homogeneous polynomial is called **$\frac{8}{7}$-Rayleigh** when it has the corresponding $\frac{8}{7}$-Rayleigh property.

**Brändén–Huh's conjecture.** The following conditions are equivalent:

1. $J$ is the set of bases of a matroid on $[n]$.
2. The generating function $f_J$ is a homogeneous $\frac{8}{7}$-Rayleigh polynomial.

The conjecture seeks an intrinsic characterization of matroid basis sets through the Rayleigh property of their generating functions. The source attributes it to Brändén and Huh; no resolution is given here.
360160.source_name: Ayush Kumar Tewari, “Positroids, Dressian and stable polynomials”, arXiv:2309.17091 (2023).
360160.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17091

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

360167.title: Local girth correspondence-colourability conjecture for planar graphs
360167.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and let $(L,M)$ be a correspondence assignment for $G$. The list assignment $L$ is a **local girth list assignment** when the list size at each vertex is determined by the girth of the relevant graph structure, as in the source.

**Local girth correspondence-colourability conjecture.** If $G$ is a planar graph and $(L,M)$ is a correspondence assignment for $G$ where $L$ is a local girth list assignment, then $G$ is $(L,M)$-colourable.

It is not currently known whether planar graphs are local girth correspondence colourable at all; this conjecture would establish that property.
360167.source_name: Luke Postle and Evelyne Smith-Roberge, “Exponentially Many Correspondence Colourings of Planar and Locally Planar Graphs”, arXiv:2309.17291 (2023).
360167.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17291

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

360183.title: The linear edge bound conjecture for k-quasiplanar graphs
360183.statement:
A **$k$-quasiplanar graph** is a graph that can be drawn in the plane with no $k$ pairwise crossing edges. **The linear edge bound conjecture.** For any $k>1$, a $k$-quasiplanar graph on $n$ vertices can have at most

$$
c_k n
$$

edges for some constant $c_k>0$. This is a long-standing conjecture about the extremal density of quasiplanar graphs; the paper does not state a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
360183.source_name: Panna Gehér and Géza Tóth, “1-planar unit distance graphs”, arXiv:2310.00940 (2025).
360183.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.00940

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2023). “Recently, his conjecture was settled by Lavoll\'ee and Swanepoel.”

360425.title: The Hotel Collatz tree conjecture
360425.statement:
Let $N$ be the set of standard reachable natural numbers, and define the directed graph $HC=\langle V,E\rangle$ by

$$
V=N,
$$

with edges

$$
E=\{\langle k,p\rangle:\exists p\;k=p+p\}\cup\{\langle k,3k+1\rangle:\exists p\;k=p+p+1\}.
$$

**Hotel Collatz conjecture.** The Hotel Collatz graph is an infinite, connected, acyclic graph, hence a tree, with $1$ as its root.

This graph-theoretic formulation recasts the Collatz iteration as a directed structure on reachable natural numbers. The supplied context gives no evidence resolving whether the graph has the asserted tree structure.
360425.source_name: Grażyna Mirkowska and Andrzej Salwicki, “Collatz conjecture becomes theorem”, arXiv:2310.13035 (2026).
360425.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.13035

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2023). “Computers are used and are still crunching numbers in the search of an eventual counterexample to the Collatz conjecture.”

360426.title: The Hotel Collatz partition conjecture
360426.statement:
Let $N$ be the set of nodes of the Hotel Collatz graph, and for each $x\in N$ let $W_x$ be the corresponding node subset. Define

$$
\overline{W}\stackrel{df}{=}\bigcup_{x\in N}W_x.
$$

**Hotel Collatz partition conjecture.** The set $\overline{W}$ is a partition of $N$.

This claim concerns a decomposition of the Hotel Collatz nodes into the sets $W_x$. The supplied context does not provide a proof or a resolution of this partition property.
360426.source_name: Grażyna Mirkowska and Andrzej Salwicki, “Collatz conjecture becomes theorem”, arXiv:2310.13035 (2026).
360426.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.13035

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2023). “Computers are used and are still crunching numbers in the search of an eventual counterexample to the Collatz conjecture.”

360432.title: Monotonicity conjecture for accurate caching-game triplets
360432.statement:
Let $v_M(n,d,k)$ and $v_A(n,d,k)$ be the values of the Multiple and Alpern Caching Games, respectively. A triplet $(n,d,k)$ is **accurate** when

$$
v_M(n,d,k)=v_A(n,d,k)=\frac{k^d}{\binom{n+d-1}{d}}.
$$

**Monotonicity conjecture.** If the integer triplet $(n,d,k)$ is accurate, then the integer triplet $(n',d',k')$ is also accurate whenever $n'\geq n$, $d'\leq d$, and $k'\leq k$.
This conjecture asserts monotonicity of accuracy under more boxes, fewer steps, and smaller query size. The supplied text gives no evidence that it has been resolved.
360432.source_name: Áron Jánosik, Csenge Miklós, Dániel G. Simon and Kristóf Zólomy, “Discrete and Continuous Caching Games”, arXiv:2310.13777 (2025).
360432.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.13777

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

360569.title: Anđelić–da Fonseca–Simić–Du conjecture on cospectral connected chain graphs
360569.statement:
Let a **chain graph** be a connected bipartite graph whose vertices in each part can be ordered by inclusion of their neighborhoods. Two graphs are **cospectral** with respect to the adjacency spectrum when their adjacency matrices have the same multiset of eigenvalues.

**Anđelić–da Fonseca–Simić–Du conjecture.** There do not exist non-isomorphic cospectral connected chain graphs with respect to the adjacency spectrum.

The conjecture concerns whether the adjacency spectrum determines a connected chain graph up to isomorphism. The paper states that it is disproved by examples with parameter $h=2$, while it holds for the class with $h=1$; thus the conjecture is refuted.
360569.source_name: Zhuang Xiong and Yaoping Hou, “On the eigenvalues and Seidel eigenvalues of chain graphs”, arXiv:2310.20230 (2023).
360569.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.20230

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of October 2023); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

360573.title: Stanley's symmetry characterization conjecture for Schur labeled skew shape posets
360573.statement:
Let $\sfP_n$ be the set of posets with underlying set $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. For $P\in\sfP_n$, let $K_P$ be its $P$-partition generating function, and let $\sfSP_n$ denote the class of Schur labeled skew shape posets.

**Stanley's symmetry characterization conjecture.** If $K_P$ is symmetric, then $P\in\sfSP_n$.

This is the implication from Stanley's broader if-and-only-if conjecture that is needed to study when modules associated with regular posets are isomorphic. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence, so the conjecture remains open here.
360573.source_name: Young-Hun Kim, So-Yeon Lee and Young-Tak Oh, “Regular Schur labeled skew shape posets and their 0-Hecke modules”, arXiv:2310.20571 (2025).
360573.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.20571

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

360574.title: Module-isomorphism conjecture for regular posets
360574.statement:
Let $\sfRP_n$ be the class of regular posets on $[n]$, let $\sfM_P$ be the associated $0$-Hecke module, and let $\Sigma_L(P)$ be the set of linear extensions of $P$. Write $\Deq$ for descent-preserving isomorphism of the relevant subsets of the symmetric group.

**Module-isomorphism conjecture.** For $P,Q\in\sfRP_n$, if

$$
\sfM_P\cong\sfM_Q,
$$

then

$$
\Sigma_L(P)\Deq\Sigma_L(Q).
$$

The conjecture seeks to extend the classification of modules from regular Schur labeled skew shape posets to all regular posets. The supplied text presents it as unresolved and provides supporting evidence from special cases.
360574.source_name: Young-Hun Kim, So-Yeon Lee and Young-Tak Oh, “Regular Schur labeled skew shape posets and their 0-Hecke modules”, arXiv:2310.20571 (2025).
360574.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.20571

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).
